subject: research/accel-surrogate
professional: a computer-architecture researcher who builds analytical and ML performance/energy models of accelerators (Timeloop/Accelergy, MAESTRO, roofline), paired with a computational-mechanics engineer for the FE side. They would check first: that the simulator's cost is counted the way a competent solver would run it (a banded beam stiffness, not a dense LU), that the surrogate is compared with the obvious cheap baselines (the closed form, a linear fit on physically motivated features), that the energy constants trace to Horowitz 2014 and include memory, that the error/gap comparison pairs each design with its own gap, and whether the 'missing question' framing is new against surrogate-modelling and quantised-inference prior work

evidence.correctness: Independent script (scratchpad accel/indep.py) recomputed: uniform cantilever PL^3/3EI by hand = 2.97619e-3 m vs fe_tip_deflection 2.97619e-3 (agrees to 1e-11); uniform shear ratio 3EI/(kGAL^2) by hand = 0.12768% = timoshenko_gap; an independent Timoshenko beam FE (shear-flexible element with phi=12EI/(kGA le^2), Przemieniecki form) over 200 random designs gives gaps within 1.45e-6 relative of the code's closed form, median 0.092%; MLP energy by hand 1312 MACs x (16 bits x 0.16 + 0.2 + 0.075) = 3719.5 pJ (code 3719.52), 6-bit 3234.1 (code 3234.08), break-even 3719.5/2.3 = 1617 flops; energy constants consistent with the Horowitz 2014 ISSCC table (8b mult 0.2 pJ, fp32 add 0.9 / mult 3.7, ~5 pJ per 32-bit 8 KB SRAM read = 0.16 pJ/bit). Rerun of experiments/run.py (25 s) reproduces every row of results.txt except QAT 4-bit (3.715/11.828 vs 3.810/12.221, run-to-run BLAS nondeterminism, inside the README's stated 0.3-point resolution). Errors found: run.py:200 takes the gap from seed 0's test designs and compares it against every seed's errors on different designs (correct pairing: float share 0.036 vs reported 0.034; small effect). The FE flop count is right for the dense np.linalg.solve the code calls, but see domain/claims.
evidence.completeness: README promises: 8 tests <1 s (pytest: 8 passed in 0.08 s; unittest Ran 8 tests in 0.039s OK), run.py about 30 s writing results.json/txt (real 25.0 s, all rows but QAT-4 identical), --report rebuild, live page https://marisstella.app/research/accel-surrogate/ (HTTP 200, title 'Can a quantised MLP surrogate of a...', stylised label present). PTQ and QAT at 3-8 bits, 5 seeds, energy and break-even all produced. RTL, 2D FE and a longer-trained model are honestly Next steps. Not linked to any programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md.
evidence.verification: 8 tests pass. Six mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: 3 caught (quantiser qmax 2^(b-1)-1 -> 2^b-1; Hermite element stiffness 4le^2 -> 3le^2; ReLU gradient > -> >=), 3 SURVIVED: Timoshenko kappa 5/6 -> 1 (beam.py:58, changes the headline gap by 17%; the only gap test asserts 0 < g < 0.1), SRAM read energy 0.16 -> 0.32 pJ/bit (cost.py:9, doubles every energy figure), dense-LU flop constant 2/3 -> 1/3 (beam.py:41, halves the headline 110x). Both headline quantities (gap and energy ratio) have no test against an independent value, and nothing pins results.txt.
evidence.craft: Read src/accel_surrogate/beam.py, mlp.py, cost.py, experiments/run.py, tests/test_surrogate.py (~300 lines). Small, readable NumPy, docstrings honest about assumptions. Defects: the gap/design pairing bug (run.py:200, res['gap'] only for seed 0, broadcast in report() at run.py:227); activation fake-quantisation qa() takes its scale from the max over the whole evaluation batch (mlp.py:18-24), i.e. calibrated on the 1000 test designs at once, which no deployed int8 engine does and which leaks test statistics; the input layer is never quantised; the 'float' row's energy is computed as a 32x8-bit integer MAC (run.py:230, bits or 32) and labelled fp; parameter count includes biases while the energy model ignores bias adds.
evidence.claims: Checked: gap median 0.09%/max 0.25% (backed), float median 1.66%/p95 4.9% (backed), PTQ deltas +0.1/+1.4/+2.1/+5.5/+21 and QAT 6-bit within 0.3 points (backed), 3.7/3.2 nJ and 1,600 break-even (backed), 'about 18 times the gap' (1.661/0.0873 = 19.0; 18 only from the rounded 0.09; partial). Not backed: 'against about 407 nJ ... roughly 110 times' (README:12): 407 nJ is a dense 2/3 n^3 LU on a 64-dof stiffness matrix with half-bandwidth 3; a banded Cholesky plus solves is ~1,920 flops (~4.4 nJ), so the ratio is ~1.2x, not 110x. The Method section does say 'dense-LU estimate ... not a profile', but the headline states 110x without that qualifier. Constants 'typed from memory' is disclosed; stylised label on page and README.
evidence.fitness: Job: an accelerator researcher wanting to know what accuracy a surrogate owes the simulator and when hardware for it pays. The chosen simulator cannot answer that: the EB tip deflection is exactly linear in the eight features 1/h_i^3 (unit-load integral, beam.py:44-53), and a least-squares fit on those features (8 MACs) trained on 3,000 designs has median test error 4e-9% (max 6e-8%), 10^7 times under the gap, while the MLP misses it by 19x. So 'the surrogate does not reach the model-form gap' is a statement about a mis-specified MLP input, not about surrogates, and the break-even conclusion holds trivially. No prior work cited on accelerator energy modelling (Timeloop/Accelergy, MAESTRO, roofline) or on surrogate quantisation; Horowitz and Jacob are the only cites. A follow-up could reuse the beam/gap code and the break-even framing, little else.
evidence.domain: Against standard practice: (1) FE cost: beam stiffness matrices are banded and every FE code solves them banded/sparse; dense 2/3 n^3 overstates the solve ~90x. (2) Energy: arithmetic-only CPU energy vs SRAM-read-inclusive accelerator energy is an apples-to-oranges comparison (Accelergy-style models charge both sides for memory); the README notes this favours the CPU, which is true, but the solve-count error goes the other way and is larger. (3) Surrogate baseline: a practitioner always tries the closed form and a physics-feature regression first. (4) Quantisation recipe (symmetric per-tensor weights, straight-through QAT after Jacob 2018) is standard and correctly implemented. The Timoshenko shear term with kappa = 5/6 for a rectangle is the textbook form and checks against an independent FE.

defects.what: Headline 'about 407 nJ ... roughly 110 times' counts the 64-dof beam solve as a dense 2/3 n^3 LU; the stiffness matrix has half-bandwidth 3, so a banded solve is ~1,920 flops (~4.4 nJ) and the FE solve is only ~1.2x the 8-bit MLP, not 110x
FE cost model fe_flops() uses dense LU for a banded system; every FE code solves beam stiffness banded/sparse

No baseline: the EB deflection is exactly linear in 1/h_i^3, and an 8-coefficient least-squares fit has 4e-9% median error vs the MLP's 1.66%, so 'the surrogate does not reach the model-form gap' reflects the MLP's input encoding, not surrogates; no prior work on accelerator modelling (Timeloop/Accelergy, MAESTRO, roofline) cited
Gap taken from seed 0's test designs only and compared against every seed's errors on different designs (share 0.034 reported vs 0.036 correctly paired)
Activation fake-quantisation scale taken from the max over the whole 1,000-design evaluation batch (test-set calibration); input layer never quantised
Headline quantities untested: kappa, SRAM read energy and the FE flop constant can all be changed with every test green; nothing pins results.txt
QAT 4-bit row does not reproduce byte-for-byte (3.715 vs 3.810 median) and README does not say runs are nondeterministic

verdict: The arithmetic is right: the EB FE, the Timoshenko gap (checked against a hand formula and an independent shear-flexible FE to 1.5e-6), and the MAC energy model all recompute, and run.py reproduces results.txt in 25 s (QAT-4 drifts within the stated resolution). The research does not hold up to an accelerator-modelling reviewer. The headline 110x energy ratio rests on a dense LU of a banded 64-dof system; banded, it is ~1.2x. The surrogate question is posed on a simulator whose output is exactly linear in 1/h^3, so an 8-MAC regression beats the gap by seven orders of magnitude and the MLP's 'miss' is a feature-encoding artefact. Three of six seeded mutants, including both headline constants, survive the tests. Finished as described, does not meet the bar.
